name: Claude Code (and Claude Agent SDK)
summary: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that reads a codebase, edits files and runs commands from the terminal, IDE extensions, a desktop app, the browser (claude.ai/code), Slack and CI; the Claude Agent SDK exposes the same loop as a Python and TypeScript library.

first_release.d: announced as a limited research preview alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet

open.d: The anthropics/claude-code repo LICENSE.md reads: (c) Anthropic PBC, all rights reserved, use subject to Anthropic's Commercial Terms. The Agent SDK is also under the Commercial Terms. The Bash sandbox runtime (@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime) is open source.

models.d: Claude models via a Claude subscription or Console API key, or through Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), Microsoft Foundry, or an LLM gateway via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Model tiers named Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku.

loop.v: main loop + subagents, plan mode, background agents, cloud sessions
loop.d: Agent tool spawns subagents with their own context window (optionally in a git worktree, background by default when fork mode is on); agent teams, dynamic Workflows, plan mode, TaskCreate/TaskUpdate task list (TodoWrite now disabled by default), parallel cloud sessions and Routines.

edit.d: Edit performs exact string replacement: old_string must match exactly and be unique unless replace_all is set; no regex or fuzzy matching. Write creates or overwrites a whole file; NotebookEdit for Jupyter cells.

context.d: Loads CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and .claude/rules/*.md up the directory tree (subdirectory files on demand); reads AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists or alongside it. Auto memory (first 200 lines or 25KB loaded). Auto-compaction near the context limit and /compact; project-root CLAUDE.md is re-read after compaction. Skills load on demand; subagents get fresh contexts.

perms.d: Permission modes default (Manual), acceptEdits, plan, auto (a background classifier reviews actions), dontAsk, bypassPermissions; allow/ask/deny rules like Bash(npm run *) and managed settings. Optional Bash sandbox uses Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap (+socat, optional seccomp) on Linux/WSL2; cloud sessions run in isolated Anthropic-managed VMs with a network allowlist and a GitHub credential proxy.

ext.v: MCP, hooks, skills, subagents, plugins, mods, Agent SDK
ext.d: Plugins bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers and a JavaScript hooks module (a plugin with one is a 'mod'), installed from marketplaces via /plugin. Agent SDK (Python, TypeScript) gives the same tools, hooks, subagents, MCP, permissions and sessions as a library.

where.v: terminal, VS Code/Cursor, JetBrains, desktop, web, mobile, Slack, CI
where.d: Terminal CLI, VS Code (and Cursor) extension, JetBrains plugin, desktop app, claude.ai/code and the mobile app (cloud sessions), Slack (@Claude), GitHub Actions (anthropics/claude-code-action@v1, triggered by @claude), GitLab CI/CD, Code Review, Routines.

price.v: Pro $20/mo and up, or API usage
price.d: As read 2026-10-05: Free has no Claude Code; Pro $20/mo ($17 annual) includes it; Max from $100/mo (5x or 20x Pro usage); Team standard $25/mo ($20 annual) and premium $125/mo ($100 annual), Claude Code in all seats; Enterprise $20/seat/mo annual plus usage at API rates; or pay-as-you-go API. Cloud sessions add no separate compute charge.

notes: Claude Agent SDK: a library that runs the Claude Code binary, in Python and TypeScript (repos anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python and -typescript), formerly the Claude Code SDK; governed by the Commercial Terms; third-party products built on it may not offer claude.ai login unless approved, so they use API keys. The GitHub Action is built on the SDK. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview

Agent SDK sits beside 'Managed Agents', a hosted harness run by Anthropic through the Claude API with sessions in an Anthropic-managed or self-hosted sandbox. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview

Recent releases 2.1.287 to 2.1.289 introduced Claude Mods (plugins with JavaScript hooks modules that can draw panes and add commands). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md
The default 'Manual' mode is the documented label for the 'default' permission mode; 'auto' mode replaces most prompts with a classifier. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions
Grep and Glob tools are absent by default on macOS, Linux and WSL in current versions (shell search is used instead). https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference

sources_read.what: tool list, Edit semantics, task tools

name: Codex
summary: OpenAI's coding agent: an open-source Rust CLI that runs locally in an OS sandbox, plus an IDE extension, the ChatGPT desktop app, cloud tasks in OpenAI-managed containers, GitHub review via @codex, and a Codex SDK.

first_release.d: openai/codex GitHub repo created 2025-04-13 (GitHub API); launch blog openai.com/index/introducing-codex returned 403 so the exact announcement date is unconfirmed

open.d: The CLI repo openai/codex is Apache-2.0 and written in Rust (codex-rs). Cloud, app and models are proprietary.

models.d: Desktop app and CLI offer Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-5.5; web offers Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna. Other providers or gateways work if they expose a compatible Responses API endpoint (configured in config.toml). Sign in with ChatGPT or use an API key.

loop.v: main thread + parallel subagents; cloud tasks
loop.d: Custom subagents are TOML files in ~/.codex/agents/ or .codex/agents/ (name, description, developer_instructions, optional model and sandbox_mode); each runs in its own thread and Codex spawns several in parallel and waits for all results. 'codex cloud' sends tasks to cloud environments and applies results locally.

edit.d: apply_patch takes a patch in OpenAI's own grammar: '*** Begin Patch', then '*** Add File:', '*** Delete File:' or '*** Update File:' (optional '*** Move to:') hunks with '@@' context lines and +/-/space lines, then '*** End Patch'. Not a unified diff; the parser is lenient for gpt-4.1.

context.d: Reads ~/.codex/AGENTS.override.md or AGENTS.md, then one file per directory from git root down to cwd (AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md, fallback names), concatenated root first, capped by project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB default). Context is compacted automatically (PreCompact/PostCompact hook events exist). Skills package repeatable instructions.

perms.d: Sandbox modes read-only, workspace-write (default), danger-full-access; approval policies on-request, never, or granular (the old 'untrusted' policy is retired). Local sandbox is Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap (bwrap) plus seccomp on Linux/WSL2, a native Windows sandbox on Windows. Cloud runs in isolated OpenAI-managed containers: setup phase has network, agent phase is offline unless internet is enabled, secrets removed before the agent phase. Rules files exist under agent configuration.

ext.v: MCP, hooks, skills, plugins, Codex SDK
ext.d: MCP servers in [mcp_servers.<name>] tables of config.toml (stdio or streamable HTTP with OAuth), or 'codex mcp add'; plugins can bundle MCP servers; hooks.json with events PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart/Stop, Stop, SessionStart/End, Interrupt; a Codex SDK.

where.v: CLI, IDE, ChatGPT desktop app, web, GitHub
where.d: CLI (macOS, Linux, Windows; 'codex exec' for CI), IDE extension for VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf, the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex web / ChatGPT Work cloud, iOS; GitHub '@codex review' and automatic PR reviews, openai/codex-action.

price.v: in ChatGPT plans from Free; or API key
price.d: As read 2026-10-05: Free $0 (basic), Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo (web, CLI, IDE, iOS), Pro $100, $200 or $500/mo (the $500 tier adds 'Astra Ultrafast'), Business $20/user/mo annual ($25 monthly, 2+ users), Enterprise and Edu custom; extra credits purchasable; API key usage billed at API rates.

notes: Docs moved: developers.openai.com/codex/* now 308-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com, and the docs frame Codex inside 'ChatGPT Work' and the ChatGPT desktop app (Chat or Work modes). https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex
The 'untrusted' approval policy has been retired; only on-request, never and granular remain. https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/agent-approvals-security
Codex Security is a separate application-security agent (plugin, CLI, SDK, cloud) and '@codex security review' exists on GitHub (research preview). https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/security
Release cadence is very fast: v0.160.1 published 2026-10-05 with 291 commits on main since. https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/latest

name: Gemini CLI
summary: Google's open-source terminal agent that brings Gemini models into the shell, with a generous free tier for anyone with a Google account.

first_release.d: announced as open source (Apache 2.0) with free Gemini 2.5 Pro access, 60 requests/min and 1,000/day

open.d: Whole CLI is open source on GitHub (google-gemini/gemini-cli); models are proprietary.

models.d: Gemini 3 family by default, other Gemini models via -m (for example gemini-2.5-flash). Auth by Google account login, Gemini API key, or Vertex AI.

loop.d: Subagents are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter in .gemini/agents/ or ~/.gemini/agents/, each with a separate context loop; built-ins codebase_investigator, cli_help, generalist, browser_agent (off by default); force with @name. The subagent docs do not mention parallel execution. Plan mode is an approval mode; remote agents are documented.

edit.d: The replace tool takes file_path, instruction, old_string, new_string and optional allow_multiple; by default exactly one occurrence must match. write_file overwrites or creates a file.

context.d: Context files default to GEMINI.md; context.fileName accepts a string or list, so AGENTS.md can be added. model.compressionThreshold triggers chat compression at a fraction of context use (default 0.5). Agent skills and an experimental auto-memory exist. Checkpointing (off by default) commits to a shadow git repo in ~/.gemini/history/<project_hash> and /restore rolls files and conversation back.

perms.d: Approval modes default, auto_edit, plan (read-only); YOLO only from the command line. Policy engine and trusted folders. Sandbox via -s/--sandbox or GEMINI_SANDBOX: macOS Seatbelt (sandbox-exec, permissive-open profile), Docker/Podman (ghcr.io/google/gemini-cli image), gVisor/runsc, experimental LXC/LXD on Linux, Windows native sandbox via icacls integrity levels.

ext.v: MCP, extensions, hooks, custom commands, skills
ext.d: Extensions bundle prompts, MCP servers, custom commands, themes, hooks, subagents and skills, installed from a GitHub URL with 'gemini extensions install'. Hooks and MCP server docs exist.

where.d: Runs in the terminal; a GitHub Action integration does PR reviews and issue triage.

price.d: As read 2026-10-05: Google account (Code Assist free) 1,000 requests/user/day; unpaid API key 250/day, Flash only; Google AI Pro 1,500/day, Ultra 2,000/day; Code Assist Standard 1,500/day, Enterprise 2,000/day; Vertex AI or paid API key pay-as-you-go.

notes: The README still quotes 60 requests/min and 1,000/day for a Google account, but the quota page now lists only 250/day (Flash only) for an unpaid API key. https://geminicli.com/docs/resources/quota-and-pricing/
The sandbox menu is the widest of the vendor CLIs: Seatbelt, Docker/Podman, gVisor, LXC and a Windows integrity-level sandbox. https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/sandbox/
Releases ship nightly, plus preview and stable channels (v0.62.0 stable on 2026-09-29). https://api.github.com/repos/google-gemini/gemini-cli/releases?per_page=3

name: Jules
summary: Google's asynchronous cloud coding agent: it clones a GitHub repo into a cloud VM, writes a plan, makes the change and opens a pull request while you do something else.

first_release.d: not on the pages fetched; web search budget was exhausted

latest.v: changelog: Gemini 3.1 Pro available in Jules

models.d: Gemini 3 Flash became the base model on 2026-01-30; Gemini 3.1 Pro for Pro plan users from 2026-03-09 (the landing page still mentions Gemini 3 Pro and 2.5 Pro).

loop.v: plan, approve, execute in a VM
loop.d: Plans then executes; a Planning Critic agent reviews auto-approved plans (2026-01-26); several tasks run concurrently (3, 15 or 60 by plan).

edit.d: Generates diffs that the user reviews before a PR is created; the internal edit tool is not documented on the pages read.

context.d: Memory file and compaction behaviour not described on the pages read.

perms.d: Runs in a Cloud VM; the user approves plans and changes before merge.

ext.d: MCP servers such as Linear, Stitch, Neon, Tinybird, Context7 and Supabase, authenticated by API keys in settings.

where.d: Web app; assign by labelling a GitHub issue 'jules'; auto-fixes CI failures on its PRs (2026-02-19).

price.d: As read 2026-10-05: Jules 15 tasks/day and 3 concurrent; Jules Pro 100/day and 15 concurrent; Jules Ultra 300/day and 60 concurrent. Prices not shown on the page.

notes: Still live, but the public changelog's newest entry is 2026-03-09, about seven months before today, so treat it as quiet rather than fast-moving. https://jules.google/docs/changelog/

name: GitHub Copilot (cloud agent, agent mode, Copilot CLI)
summary: GitHub's AI coding assistant across VS Code and other IDEs, the terminal (Copilot CLI), a Copilot app and github.com, where the Copilot cloud agent takes an assigned issue, works in an ephemeral GitHub Actions environment and opens a pull request.
status: active (the 'coding agent' is now documented as 'Copilot cloud agent')

first_release.d: coding agent public preview for Pro+ and Enterprise: assign an issue, runs in a GitHub Actions powered environment

latest.v: Copilot CLI v1.0.92; changelog 'Dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app'

open.d: The copilot-cli repo LICENSE.md is a custom 'GitHub Copilot CLI License' allowing install and unmodified redistribution only (not MIT, despite what a summary of the README suggested). Service is proprietary.

models.d: Models from OpenAI (GPT-5.x, GPT-6 Astra/Luna/Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol), Anthropic (Claude Fable 5/5.1, Opus 4.8/5/5.5, Sonnet 4.6/5/5.5, Haiku 4.5), Google (Gemini 3.7/3.8 Flash), Microsoft (MAI-Code-1.1-Flash), Moonshot (Kimi K3), xAI (Grok 4.5 to 4.7); GPT-5.3-Codex is the long-term fallback. VS Code can also run Anthropic Claude and OpenAI harnesses.

loop.v: agent mode, plan mode, autopilot, subagents, cloud agent
loop.d: Cloud agent: one repo, one branch, one PR per task, max 59 minutes per session. VS Code has #agent/runSubagent and #todos; Copilot CLI has plan mode, autopilot mode, custom agents in ~/.copilot/agents or .github/agents, and dynamic workflows (2026-10-01).

edit.v: #edit/editFiles (VS Code); CLI edit tool not documented
edit.d: VS Code exposes #edit/editFiles, #edit/createFile, #edit/editNotebook; the pages read do not give the underlying edit format.

context.d: Repository-wide .github/copilot-instructions.md, path-specific .github/instructions/NAME.instructions.md (cloud agent and code review), agent instructions AGENTS.md (nearest wins), CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md at repo root. CLI auto-compresses at 95% of context (/compact).

perms.d: CLI: per-use or session approvals, --allow-tool, --deny-tool (wins), --allow-all-tools, trusted directories. Local sandbox (/sandbox enable): Seatbelt on macOS 15+, bubblewrap 0.5+ on Linux, Windows ProcessContainer BaseContainer tier. Cloud sandbox on Azure Container Apps Sandboxes. Cloud agent runs in GitHub Actions behind a default-on firewall allowlist that covers only processes started by its Bash tool, not MCP servers.

ext.d: CLI ships GitHub's MCP server by default and accepts custom MCP servers; hooks, skills, custom agents and custom instructions; cloud agent supports repository MCP configuration.

where.v: IDE, CLI, Copilot app, github.com, Mobile
where.d: VS Code (local, background and cloud sessions) and other IDEs, Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, github.com (assign issues, code review), GitHub Mobile.

price.v: AI Credits: Free, Pro $10, Pro+ $39, Max $100
price.d: As read 2026-10-05: Free $0 (limited chat and agent), Pro $10/mo with $15 of AI Credits, Pro+ $39/mo with $70, Max $100/mo with $200; 1 credit = $0.01, more purchasable; coding agent and CLI in all. Business and Enterprise listed without prices on the page read. Premium requests are now a legacy model for subscribers who stayed on it after 2026-06-01; cloud agent also uses Actions minutes.

notes: Billing changed from premium requests to GitHub AI Credits: the premium-request article is now labelled for legacy subscribers who remained on request-based billing after 2026-06-01. https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/billing/copilot-requests
Renamed: the 'Copilot coding agent' is now called 'Copilot cloud agent' in the docs. https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/coding-agent/customize-the-agent-firewall
Copilot CLI is not open source: its licence is a custom GitHub Copilot CLI License. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/copilot-cli/main/LICENSE.md
The CLI README still names Claude Sonnet 4.5 as the default model, which looks stale next to the current models page. https://github.com/github/copilot-cli
New 'Max' individual plan at $100/mo; Copilot can now use computer use on desktop apps (2026-10-01). https://github.com/features/copilot/plans https://github.blog/changelog/

name: Amp
maker: Amp Frontier Corporation (spun out of Sourcegraph, 2025-12-08)
summary: A frontier coding agent and cloud dev environment where every thread can run in its own remote machine (an 'orb') or on your own computer (a 'runner'), driven from the web, a CLI, and macOS and iOS apps.
status: acquired-out / spun out: now an independent company; editor extensions killed in 2026

first_release.d: 'Amp Is Now Available To Everyone' (after a research preview with posts from 2025-04)

open.d: Hosted service plus a closed single-file CLI binary (formerly the npm package @sourcegraph/amp); no source licence found on the pages read.

models.v: Amp-chosen frontier models per mode; bring your own via model routing
models.d: Modes low, medium, high, ultra each bundle a model, effort, prompt, tools and oracle (GPT-6 Astra powers the High mode per the Plaid post; Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 posts in Sept 2026). Model routing lets you send traffic through your own API keys (Anthropic, Google AI Studio, Meta AI, OpenAI, xAI), subscriptions (ChatGPT, SuperGrok), Bedrock or Google Cloud Agent Platform, or gateways (OpenRouter, Vercel, Cloudflare, Ollama Cloud and others).

loop.v: threads with specialist subagents, running in orbs
loop.d: Subagents Search, Oracle (hard reasoning and planning), Librarian (external codebases on GitHub), Read Thread, each with isolated context; plugins can add custom modes and subagents. Every thread can get its own orb that keeps working after you close the laptop, with automations and event-driven wake-ups.

edit.d: Built-in tools are listed only by 'amp tools list'; the docs pages read do not name the edit tool or its format.

context.v: AGENTS.md everywhere; Handoff instead of compaction
context.d: Reads AGENTS.md in cwd and parents up to $HOME, subtree files on demand, plus $HOME/.config/amp/AGENTS.md and system-wide files (/etc/ampcode/AGENTS.md etc.). In Oct 2025 Amp removed /compact and replaced it with Handoff (start a new thread with selected context); threads can read other threads. Skills and global plugins exist.

perms.v: no approvals by default; isolation by orb
perms.d: 'Amp does not ask for approval before running tools' by default; control comes from a custom plugin (workspace admins can distribute one). Orbs are isolated remote machines per thread (virtualisation technology not disclosed), with OIDC grants for production access.

ext.v: plugins (Plugin API), skills, MCP, SDK, API
ext.d: Plugins via a Plugin API (can define modes, subagents and tool-use policy), skills, remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP with OAuth or bearer tokens (usable in orbs, TUI and Puck), an SDK and an API.

where.v: web, CLI, macOS and iOS apps, Slack (Puck)
where.d: Threads open in the web app, the CLI and the iOS/macOS apps; agents run in orbs, on runners (amp --no-tui on any machine, including your Mac) or locally. Puck has a Slack integration. VS Code and Cursor extensions were killed in Feb 2026.

price.v: free with BYO model and compute; pay for orbs or inference
price.d: As read 2026-10-05: Hobby free with all features and no BYOK token fees (since 2026-09-13); $20/mo plan includes 45,000 orb minutes; Teams at no extra charge with pooled credits; Enterprise custom. Inference through Amp at cost with no markup. Orbs billed per minute, from a1.tiny $0.08/h to a1.3xlarge $2.13/h, paused orbs free.

notes: 2025-12-08: 'Amp is becoming a separate company', spun out of Sourcegraph as Amp Frontier Corporation, described as profitable; Sourcegraph is now listed among its investors. https://ampcode.com/news/amp-frontier-corporation
2026-02-19 'The Coding Agent Is Dead': Amp killed its VS Code and Cursor extensions to unshackle models from the editor. https://ampcode.com/news/the-coding-agent-is-dead

Ad-supported 'Amp Free' (Oct 2025, $10/day of credits) reached a $10M+ ad run rate, then dropped ads on 2026-03-30 and is now paused; since 2026-09-13 Amp is free with your own keys or ChatGPT subscription and charges for orbs. https://ampcode.com/news/amp-free-is-ad-free https://ampcode.com/news/free-agent
Amp replaced compaction with Handoff in Oct 2025, arguing compaction is lossy; a clean teaching contrast with Claude Code and Codex auto-compaction. https://ampcode.com/news/handoff
The old smart/rush/deep/free modes have been replaced by a four-step Dial (low, medium, high, ultra). https://ampcode.com/docs/the-dial

name: Kiro CLI (formerly Amazon Q Developer CLI)
summary: AWS's terminal coding agent, the renamed successor of the Amazon Q Developer CLI, sharing credits, models, steering files and custom agents with the Kiro IDE.
status: renamed: Amazon Q Developer CLI became Kiro CLI (available 2025-11-17, auto-update 2025-11-24)

first_release.d: Kiro CLI available; q and q chat entry points still work, config moves from ~/.aws/amazonq to ~/.kiro

open.d: The Q Developer CLI was Apache 2.0; Kiro CLI moved to the proprietary AWS IP License.

models.d: GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Claude Opus 5 and 5.5 (experimental), Sonnet 5 and 5.5, open-weight MiniMax M2.5, GLM-5, DeepSeek 3.2, Qwen3 Coder Next at credit multipliers down to 0.05x, plus an Auto router.

loop.d: Sub-agents 'run in parallel'; custom agents; opt-in multi-step workflows and workflow delegation (CLI 2.26 to 2.27); headless mode.

edit.d: Permissions name the capabilities fs_read, fs_write, shell, web_fetch, mcp; the edit format of fs_write is not documented on the pages read.

context.d: Steering markdown in .kiro/steering/ and ~/.kiro/steering/ with inclusion modes Always, FileMatch, Manual, Auto (all four in CLI V3); AGENTS.md at workspace root, in subdirectories or in ~/.kiro/steering/ is always included. Compaction exists but was not detailed on the page read.

perms.d: YAML permissions.yaml at user and workspace scope with effects deny, ask, allow over capabilities and glob patterns; most restrictive wins across Kiro, admin, user, workspace, agent and session scopes; untrusted workspaces add prompts. No OS sandbox mentioned.

ext.v: MCP, custom agents, saved prompt commands
ext.d: MCP servers; custom agents; saved prompts as slash commands (CLI 2.27.0).

where.d: kiro-cli in the terminal (chat, headless, voice); the Kiro IDE is a sibling product sharing the plan.

price.d: As read 2026-10-05: Free $0 / 50 credits; Pro $20 / 1,000; Pro+ $40 / 2,000; Pro Max $100 / 5,000; Power $200 / 10,000 per user per month; overage $0.04/credit; CLI in all tiers; Q Developer subscriptions keep working.

notes: Why include: it is the renamed Amazon Q Developer CLI, so anyone who knew 'Q CLI' needs the new name, and the rename came with a licence change from Apache 2.0 to a proprietary AWS licence. https://kiro.dev/docs/upgrade-guides/migrating-from-q/

name: Qwen Code
summary: Alibaba's open-source terminal coding agent, forked from Gemini CLI and now developed independently, that works with Qwen models or any OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or local endpoint.

first_release.d: GitHub repo QwenLM/qwen-code created (GitHub API); based on Gemini CLI v0.8.2, independent from Qwen Code v0.1

open.d: Framework is Apache-2.0 and the README stresses that the Qwen models are open too.

models.d: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen API protocols, switchable at runtime; Alibaba ModelStudio (Coding Plan, Token Plan) recommended; third parties such as DeepSeek, Grok, MiniMax, Z.AI, Kimi, OpenRouter; local Ollama or vLLM.

loop.d: README lists SubAgents, Agent Teams, Dynamic Workflows, Git worktrees, and an 'Agent Arena' that runs several models head-to-head on one task.

edit.d: Edit tool not described on the pages read (it inherits Gemini CLI's code base, but that was not verified today).

context.v: Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills; context file name unconfirmed
context.d: README lists Auto-Memory and Auto-Skills; the auth page did not name the context file.

perms.d: Five modes cycled with Shift+Tab; Auto uses an LLM classifier to approve safe shell, network and out-of-workspace actions (like Claude Code's auto mode). A sandbox exists per the README; its technology was not stated on the pages read.

ext.v: MCP, hooks, skills, SDKs, ACP daemon
ext.d: MCP, hooks, built-in skills (/review, /batch, /loop, /bugfix), LSP; SDKs in TypeScript, Python and Java; 'qwen serve' daemon over HTTP + SSE (ACP).

where.v: terminal, IDEs, desktop, web UI, chat apps
where.d: Terminal, VS Code, Zed and JetBrains, a desktop app, an experimental web UI, Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat, Feishu; headless 'qwen -p' for CI.

price.v: free software; pay your model provider
price.d: As read 2026-10-05: the agent is free; the Qwen OAuth free tier ended 2026-04-15, so users pay via Alibaba ModelStudio Coding or Token Plan (prices not on the page) or another provider.

notes: Why include: the most visible open-source vendor CLI from a Chinese lab, an example of forking Gemini CLI, and it publishes per-version SWE-bench Verified scores of its harness (about 76 to 78% with Qwen 3.7 Max), useful for teaching harness-vs-model effects. https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code
Free Qwen OAuth tier (formerly a big draw) was discontinued on 2026-04-15. https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/auth/
